provenance.why_by_hand: Both automatic band readers written this round (_jp5band.mjs absolute-ink, _jp5band-v2.mjs local-angular-variance) reported themselves AT a search bound on this coin (COIN-JUDGE.md 4.1) because the memorial's relief on the reverse and the bust on the obverse run inboard of the legend with no bare gutter between. Appendix R3: a detector's failure is not the artefact's failure, and 2.1: a hand annotation read off the source is a legitimate frozen target.

convention.units: viewBox units, X = 50 + 47 (px - cx) / R, so the coin's own silhouette is r = 47 BY CONSTRUCTION
convention.rOuter: radius of the legend's extreme nearest the RIM
convention.rInner: radius of the legend's extreme nearest the CENTRE
convention.note: rOuter/rInner are used instead of baseline/cap-top on purpose. A top legend has its typographic baseline at rInner and a bottom legend has it at rOuter, and judge/_jq4band.json (the quarter's) records the bottom legend as baseline 37.0 cap-top 43.7, i.e. with the opposite convention to the physical one. Naming the extremes removes the trap.

edge_check.method: _jp7edge.mjs: per angular column, radius of max |d grey / d r| in the window 44..49; median over 1800 columns

ONE CENT.span_deg_corrected_2026_08_22: was 136. Judge ruling: it did not reproduce. The same instrument, on the same file, at the same frozen disc, reads 113.0 while reproducing this entry's neighbours to two decimals; three references bracket 113/119/124. And the record contradicted ITSELF: with its own cap 10.4 at its own rOuter 41.3, any plausible letter advance (0.85-1.15x cap) gives 98-133 deg of ink, with 113 landing at almost exactly 1.0x cap, while 136 needs 1.18x. The drawing was corrected to match the coin and failed only this stale target.
